title: Invergent Health - Renewal & Expansion Roadmap Review
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on contract extension options, adding EU region and a private VPC pilot, and validating performance targets and SR latency. Customer wants a 12-month extension with a phased capacity uplift and a short on-prem-like pilot. Security team requested KMS/HSM details and audit log retention. Action: Redwood to send revised SOW, security pack, and run a 48-hour latency/cost benchmark against their 2k QPS mixed workload.
topics: EU region activation and data residency
Private VPC pilot vs Dedicated pool
Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence
action_items: Leah Ortiz: Share current traffic profile (p95 p99, seq length dist) - due 2025-07-18
Jordan Patel: Send revised SOW with phased capacity uplift and pricing options (12/24 mo) - due 2025-07-17
Maya Chen: Schedule 48h benchmark run and provide test harness; share expected metrics template - due 2025-07-20
Owen Brooks: Provide security pack (KMS/HSM integration details, retention, SOC2 evidence) - due 2025-07-16
next_steps: Redwood to run benchmark in customer staging with sample workload (48 hours)
Customer to review SOW and confirm preferred term by 2025-07-22
Set follow-up contractual review meeting for pricing alignment (week of 2025-07-21)
Security deep-dive with Invergent's security team the week after SOW signoff
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-15 14:30 UTC, Duration ~48m, Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Owen (Redwood CSM), Dr Samir (CTO), Leah (MLOps), Marcus (VP Product), Nia (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick check-in agenda; renewal options, EU onramp, private VPC pilot ask from Nia, and then benchmarking. Sound right?
[00:18] Dr Samir: Yep that's it. We're roughly on the same page. Wanted to see numbers and timeline, and make sure security is satisfied before we commit to a longer term.
[00:28] Leah: Also want to reconcile latency targets - our app is sensitive to p99 spikes. We're seeing occasional elevation at peak hours.
[00:35] Jordan: Totally. For context, we prepared two options: a 12-month extension with phased capacity uplift and a 24-month term with discounting and reserved burst capacity. I'll walk the pricing after we iron out the technical asks.
[00:48] Marcus: Quick one — what's the difference operationally if we go Dedicated vs Private VPC? Leah and Nia are worried about data paths and egress.
[01:02] Maya: Good question. Dedicated is a reserved pool in Redwood's cloud with tenant isolation; Private VPC brings the control plane into your VPC and network level controls, and on-prem option is also doable but it's a heavier lift. For EU residency, Private VPC or on-prem is the stronger compliance posture.
[01:23] Nia: For us KMS + HSM proofs and audit log retention windows are critical. We need to see integration patterns — ideally we manage keys via our KMS.
[01:33] Owen: We can supply a security pack; we integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS/GCP) and have HSM-assisted key material for private deployments. We'll include SOC 2 attestation artifacts.
[01:45] Nia: Okay, but retention — what's the default? 30 days? 90? We need logs retained for six months for some internal audits.
[01:55] Owen: Default audit retention is 90 days in hosted, but for enterprise Private we can offer extended retention as an add-on to match your six months. We'll detail that in the pack.
[02:10] Leah: Back to performance: our token distribution is mixed — short prompts for classification and multi-turn chat for assistants. We'll send a workload profile. Can you support continuous KV cache reuse and prefix caching? Our previous setup had cold cache latency spikes.
[02:28] Maya: Yep, runtime supports prefix/KV caching and ongoing batching. We'll need the seq length histogram to tune batching windows and kernel selection. Also we'd recommend a quantization profile for the chat models to reduce cost while keeping quality.
[02:44] Dr Samir: That brings up accuracy risk with quantization. We can't degrade clinical summary fidelity. How do you measure regressions?
[02:54] Jordan: We couple evals with release rollouts — we can run your golden prompt set against candidate quantized variants and show per-prompt deltas. Redwood Optimize can flag regression alerts tied to eval sets.
[03:10] Marcus: Can we talk EU region activation? We'd like Ireland initially and then maybe Germany for data locality.
[03:18] Maya: Ireland is available; Germany is on roadmap but we'd need timeline commitments. Activation typically takes ~2-4 weeks for a reserved region depending on capacity. For Private VPC in EU it'll be a bit longer — 4-8 weeks — because of network and KMS integration.
[03:36] Leah: Cost delta for Private VPC vs Dedicated? Rough ballpark.
[03:40] Jordan: Private VPC has a platform fee + infra, think ~15-25% uplift over equivalent Dedicated pool in most cases, but you get the residency and network control. Longer commitments (24mo) lower the uplift materially. We'll show concrete numbers in the SOW.
[03:58] Nia: Any fallback or failover patterns if the EU nodes have capacity contention? We need graceful degradation.
[04:06] Maya: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible model in another region or route to lower latency zones, with metrics-based failover. You can pin fallbacks per route.
[04:20] Speaker 1: (inaudible) tests on requests per second — what does 2k QPS look like for you?
[04:26] Jordan: 2k QPS mixed workload is substantial but we've run similar. For that profile we'd plan a Dedicated pool with autoscale and burst buffer. The benchmark plan we propose is a 48-hour run against a staging mirror of your traffic.
[04:40] Leah: We'll provide a hashed traffic profile. We need to see p95/p99 and token cost per inference.
[04:47] Maya: We'll capture latency distribution, tokens per request, GPU utilization, and cost-per-token with and without prefix caching. We'll share the runbook and harness.
[05:02] Marcus: On contracts — if we commit to 24 months, can we get guaranteed throughput SLAs? We want p99 under 350ms for short single-turn prompts.
[05:12] Jordan: SLA tiers are negotiable with Dedicated/Private contracts. We can commit to p99 targets with appropriate provisioned capacity and penalties. Let's model the SLA once we have the benchmark numbers.
[05:26] Dr Samir: Budget constraint — we have to show cost savings vs our current provider who does some self-hosting; show us unit economics.
[05:33] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll include a comparative sheet. Also our Optimize toolkit will recommend batching/quantization combos to hit cost targets.
[05:45] Nia: About data flow: in Private VPC, does traffic ever traverse Redwood-managed control plane outside EU? We have strict data residency rules.
[05:53] Maya: Control plane metadata needs limited contact to Redwood for control-plane ops unless you choose an on-prem control plane option. For full isolation we can route control-plane traffic through your VPC endpoints and give tighter egress controls; we will describe the options.
[06:10] Leah: What's the typical lead time to increase capacity by 2x? We might need quick top-ups during campaign spikes.
[06:17] Owen: For Dedicated pools with burst capacity enabled, you can autoscale across queued capacity; top-ups can be near real-time (minutes) up to configured burst limits. Reserved literal capacity increases in days depending on availability.
[06:32] Marcus: Any gotchas with our inference patterns (mixed short and long seqs)?
[06:36] Maya: Mixed sequences mean batching strategies must be workload-aware. We may recommend separate routes for short-turn classification vs long-chat to avoid head-of-line latency. Also KV cache tuning is critical for multi-turn.
[06:50] Dr Samir: About benchmarks — can Redwood run them inside our staging VPC? We prefer tests in our network to capture egress and real-world latencies.
[06:58] Maya: We can run the benchmark from your staging if you provide a test endpoint and keys; we will need a short onboarding for the harness. Otherwise we can mirror your traffic in Redwood staging but your network characteristics won't be identical.
[07:14] Leah: We'll give you a staging endpoint. Expect a redacted dataset for PII. We'll hash IDs.
[07:21] Jordan: Sounds good. Next, timelines — proposed SOW delivery tomorrow, benchmark next week; decision by 2025-07-22.
[07:29] Dr Samir: That's tight but doable. If the benchmark looks good, we'd be fine with a 12mo clearly spelled phased uplift. With security sign-off maybe 24mo for better economics.
[07:42] Nia: We want an architecture diagram for Private VPC showing KMS handshake, audit log flow, and retention paths. Also a table of compliance evidence.
[07:52] Owen: We'll include diagrams and SOC2 + ISO docs in the pack.
[08:00] Jordan: Any other blockers?
[08:03] Marcus: One more — error budgets and observability; does Console expose token-level cost per route? Can we export traces?
[08:12] Maya: Yes, Console gives per-route token cost, latency breakdowns, traces. You can export via API or SIEM integration. We'll send sample dashboard screenshots.
[08:24] Leah: Great. That helps us build the internal ROI case.
[08:28] Jordan: Okay to recap action items — we'll send SOW, security pack, and Maya will kick off benchmark once Leah provides traffic. Owen will follow-up on retention.
[08:39] Dr Samir: Good. If we like the bench numbers, who signs the SOW? Myself and procurement loop.
[08:45] Jordan: Typically procurement signs after legal review; we'll support with a procurement checklist.
[08:52] Speaker 2: (background) Can we get a quick note on pricing delta for EU region?
[08:57] Jordan: High level: EU region add is a per-region activation fee plus slightly higher infra cost due to smaller infra pools. We'll quantify in SOW.
[09:10] Marcus: Any recommended mitigation for hallucination-sensitive prompts? We need conservative generation for summaries.
[09:16] Maya: We'll recommend model selection with safety configs, response filtration and a deterministic decoding profile for summaries. Also can add model ensembles for verification.
[09:28] Leah: Good. Please include a proposed rollout plan for canary traffic split and A/B evaluation of quantized candidates.
[09:35] Maya: We'll include a canary rollout playbook with rollback thresholds and automatic fallback to unfuzzed models.
[09:44] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll send the SOW and schedule the benchmark run. Anything else before we close?
[09:49] Dr Samir: No, that's it. Thanks.

(End of recording)
notes: Customer leaning toward 12-month with option to convert to 24-month after successful pilot
Security retention and KMS integration are gating items
Benchmark will be the primary decider for SLA and final pricing
